method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Association of Urology (EAU) 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)' (limited update March 2026). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. The source's words are NOT reproduced here. The guideline's terms also state (verbatim): 'the EAU prohibits the usage or upload of its Guidelines, and any material derived from these texts (whether in full or in part) on external websites, bots, pages, portals, servers, software or external applications, including those employing artificial intelligence technologies and infrastructure, such as large language models and generative AI, deep learning and machine learning, unless written permission has been granted for such by the EAU.' Recorded per the standing owner decision (Wave 4); the content is paraphrased and hash-anchored.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Autonomic dysreflexia is an emergency to recognise:** it usually occurs with spinal cord lesions at or above T6 and is defined by a rise in systolic pressure of more than 20 mmHg over baseline, typically with severe headache, blurred vision and flushing and sweating above the lesion. A full bladder or bowel or an indwelling catheter can set it off, and it can be fatal if poorly managed.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diagnose and treat early,** in both congenital and acquired neurological disease, to stop permanent damage to the urinary tract.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Take a history of all four functions (bladder, bowel, sexual and neurological)** and look for alarm features such as pain, infection, haematuria or fever that need their own work-up. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Baseline and routine tests:** urinalysis, blood chemistry, a bladder diary, post-void residual, a measure of leakage, and imaging of the urinary tract. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Urodynamics is the only objective test of lower urinary tract function.** Do non-invasive tests first; for invasive studies use video-urodynamics, or if unavailable a filling cystometry that continues into a pressure-flow study. Monitor blood pressure and heart rate in anyone at risk of autonomic dysreflexia. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The kidneys are at risk, especially when the bladder fills at high pressure.** Spinal cord injury and spina bifida carry more risk of renal failure than slowly progressive conditions such as MS or Parkinson's disease. With low muscle mass, a cystatin C-based GFR detects kidney disease better than a creatinine-based estimate.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Priorities, in order: protect the upper tracts, achieve continence, restore lower tract function, and improve quality of life.** Holding bladder pressure within safe limits during filling and voiding is the top priority, because it cuts deaths from urological causes.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **When the bladder is overactive or poorly compliant, the aim is a low-pressure reservoir,** even if that leaves residual urine.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Discourage Credé (suprapubic pressure) and Valsalva straining** unless urodynamics shows bladder pressure stays safe: the pressures are harmful to the urinary tract, and these methods can worsen stress incontinence.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Triggered reflex voiding can also generate high pressure and can provoke autonomic dysreflexia in high spinal injuries,** so patients need training and close urodynamic follow-up.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Never use a penile clamp with detrusor overactivity or low compliance:** it raises bladder pressure and risks pressure necrosis where sensation is reduced.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For neurogenic overactive bladder, use an antimuscarinic or a beta-3 agonist;** antimuscarinics are first-line for detrusor overactivity. Do not choose a beta-3 agonist to lower urodynamically proven overactivity, which it does not improve. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **For poor emptying caused by outlet resistance, prescribe an α-blocker** (examples given: tamsulosin, naftopidil, silodosin); these lower outlet resistance, residual volume and autonomic dysreflexia. (Strong) See the banner on phenoxybenzamine, the PBS drug.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not use parasympathomimetics (such as bethanechol) for an underactive detrusor.** (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Intermittent catheterisation, by the patient or a carer, is the preferred method** when a neurological patient cannot empty the bladder. Sterile technique is not routine, and people need careful counselling before they start.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Typical practice: catheterise four to six times a day with a 12–16 Fr catheter, keeping each drained volume to no more than 400–500 mL.** Hydrophilic catheters are linked with fewer UTIs.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid indwelling urethral and, to a lesser degree, suprapubic catheters where possible,** because of complications and infection. If one is needed, prefer silicone (less encrustation, and latex allergy is common in this group); intermittent clamping brings no benefit. Investigate standard bladder-cancer red flags promptly in long-term catheter users.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Decide between intermittent and indwelling catheters with the patient,** and teach the technique and its risks thoroughly. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If antimuscarinics fail, inject botulinum toxin A into the detrusor** to reduce neurogenic overactivity. (Strong) The effect wears off after about nine months and repeat injections keep working.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Urinary retention is a common adverse effect, so intermittent catheterisation may become necessary,** particularly in MS, where patients often do not catheterise beforehand; a 100 U dose may lower that need in MS.
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not screen with urine dipsticks, and neither look for nor treat bacteriuria without symptoms,** in neurological patients. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For recurrent UTIs, first improve bladder management and remove foreign bodies such as stones or indwelling catheters.** Avoid continuous long-term antibiotics; weekly cycling of antibiotic prophylaxis can be offered to selected spinal cord injury patients who self-catheterise. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow up for life, tailored to risk:** in high-risk patients check the upper tracts and repeat urodynamics at regular intervals, and investigate any significant clinical change with a specialist. (Strong)
claims.locator: European Association of Urology (EAU), 'EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (limited update March 2026)', limited update March 2026, https://d56bochluxqnz.cloudfront.net/documents/full-guideline/EAU-Guidelines-on-Neuro-Urology-2026.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23
